ultrasound.title: Tenth thoracic vertebra · ultrasound orientation · draft
ultrasound.body: On a posterior thoracic sonogram, first separate the midline spinous-process echo from the adjacent laminar echoes. The bright accessible cortex casts a deeper acoustic shadow; the shadow is not a view through the vertebral body.
bullets: Moving laterally in the anatomy changes the expected bony landmark from lamina and articular column to transverse process, costotransverse region and rib. A rib echo and its shadow should not be renamed as the selected vertebra.

Ribs and overlapping posterior elements leave restricted interlaminar acoustic gaps. In an adult volunteer study, upper thoracic views were more often inconclusive than lower thoracic views; even a visible gap does not make the whole canal visible.

A thoracic level label requires a verified counting context. Rib number or a single prominent process can mislead where thoracolumbar segments or rib counts vary; this isolated bone surface cannot resolve an individual patient’s vertebral numbering.

anatomy.body: The central canal is the small ependymal-lined lumen described within the central spinal-cord region. In adult humans, a continuous open lumen is often absent; the reference surface is not evidence of patency at every level.
bullets: Central canal representation only, not the surrounding cord, axons or spinal nerves. No fluid dynamics, lumen measurements, syrinx diagnosis or regenerative-cell function is established by this model.

ct.title: Central canal of spinal cord · CT: distinguish the spaces · draft
ct.body: The central canal belongs within the spinal cord; it is not the larger vertebral canal enclosing the cord. Do not label the bony canal on CT as this small intramedullary space. A visible atlas surface does not establish that the normal central canal can be resolved on routine CT.
bullets: CT myelography outlines the cord and nerve roots using contrast in the surrounding subarachnoid space. That contrast column is not a cast of the central canal.
MRI is used to assess the cord itself and suspected intramedullary cavities. This anatomical model supplies neither CT attenuation nor a diagnostic exclusion of cord disease.

mri.title: Central canal of spinal cord · MRI: a canal-like signal is not a diagnosis · draft
mri.body: A thin fluid-signal feature within or near the midline of the cord needs anatomical interpretation, not automatic labelling as a syrinx. MRI is the principal imaging method for evaluating syringomyelia, but this source surface is a reference representation, not a segmented cavity from that examination.
bullets: Petit-Lacour and colleagues described appearances compatible with a persistent central canal in 12 of 794 spinal MRI studies. That observational series does not supply a universal size threshold or a patient-specific diagnosis.

An exploratory cervical MRI study found that some canal-like T2 signal may relate to the anterior median fissure. Compare axial and sagittal relationships; a sagittal bright line alone does not establish the precise space.
Do not infer patency, fluid flow, symptoms or treatment from this mesh. Any proposed scan correspondence needs the actual acquisition, annotation and revision-bound radiologist review.

bullets: The normal disc series begins below the axis, at C2–C3; there is no intervertebral disc between atlas and axis. Disc joints are distinct from the posterior synovial facet joints.

Compare the selected disc with the neighbouring bodies as a functional unit, without assigning a patient imaging interval from its source name.
Posture and load matter to the cervical stress pattern; lumbar mechanics cannot simply be carried over to this region.
The study measured cadaveric behaviour. This static surface cannot show stress within the selected disc or predict an individual response.
The axis source label refers to a disc below C2. There is no C1–C2 intervertebral disc.

function.title: Intervertebral disk of second thoracic vertebra · Function · draft
function.body: This source-labelled thoracic disc contributes to load transfer within the thoracic column. An in-vitro study found that disc pressure varied with loading direction and segmental region.
bullets: Intervertebral discs are fibrocartilaginous joints between vertebral bodies. An outer annulus surrounds an inner nucleus; together they help cushion and distribute load while allowing movement between bodies.
A thoracic disc should be considered with its surrounding vertebral and rib-cage context, rather than as an isolated spacer.
The tested pressure pattern depended on direction and region; one fixed value would obscure those differences.
The experiment retained short rib stumps rather than an intact rib cage, so it does not supply universal motion or force claims for patients.

function.title: Intervertebral disk of fifth thoracic vertebra · Function · draft
function.body: This source-labelled thoracic disc contributes to load transfer within the thoracic column. An in-vitro study found that disc pressure varied with loading direction and segmental region.
bullets: Intervertebral discs are fibrocartilaginous joints between vertebral bodies. An outer annulus surrounds an inner nucleus; together they help cushion and distribute load while allowing movement between bodies.
A thoracic disc should be considered with its surrounding vertebral and rib-cage context, rather than as an isolated spacer.
The tested pressure pattern depended on direction and region; one fixed value would obscure those differences.
The experiment retained short rib stumps rather than an intact rib cage, so it does not supply universal motion or force claims for patients.

The experiment retained short rib stumps rather than an intact rib cage, so it does not supply universal motion or force claims for patients.

function.title: Intervertebral disk of fifth lumbar vertebra · Function · draft
function.body: This source-labelled lumbar disc helps distribute loads between vertebral bodies. A cadaveric study found that internal load sharing changed with tissue condition.
bullets: Intervertebral discs are fibrocartilaginous joints between vertebral bodies. An outer annulus surrounds an inner nucleus; together they help cushion and distribute load while allowing movement between bodies.
The annulus and nucleus contribute differently to load sharing, even though this whole-disc surface does not separate them.
Changes in tissue condition can alter the internal response to a load; an external outline alone cannot quantify pressure.
The cadaveric findings explain a mechanical principle, not the condition or performance of this selected source mesh or any patient disc.
function.note: The 22 selections are whole-disc surfaces: annulus, nucleus and endplates are not independently segmented, and one source level remains unresolved. Source names do not automatically assign a two-vertebra patient imaging interval. Mesh shape, cutaway and explode provide no numerical pressure, strain, motion, diagnosis or CT/MR registration. Revision-bound radiologist review is pending. Case, Atlas and lecture access remain independent.

mri.title: Intervertebral disk of fifth lumbar vertebra · MRI orientation · draft
mri.body: On acquired sagittal and axial MRI, confirm the lumbar disc level, then follow its posterior and lateral contour from the central canal through the subarticular zone (lateral recess) to the neural foramen and extraforaminal region. Describe the observed location separately from any neural finding.
bullets: Compare adjacent sections and both planes: a central or subarticular finding and a foraminal or extraforaminal finding occupy different regions, even when they arise from the same disc.

As a regional principle, a subarticular finding may relate to a traversing root, while a foraminal or extraforaminal finding may relate to an exiting root. Confirm the patient level, side and actual root course; the source label cannot assign a root in a patient.

Consensus nomenclature separates a generalized disc bulge from localized herniation, with protrusion and extrusion describing herniation shapes. Apply those terms only to acquired images; neither morphology nor proximity alone establishes symptom causation.
